title: How to Fix Common Windows Update Errors
description: Work through practical checks for stuck downloads, failed updates, and repeated Windows Update errors.
intro: Windows updates can fail because of a temporary service issue, low storage, damaged system files, or a connection problem. Start with low-risk checks and move on only when needed.

steps.heading: Restart and check the basics
steps.body: Save your work and restart the PC. Confirm the internet connection is stable and date and time are correct. Disconnect a VPN temporarily if it appears to interrupt the update, then retry.

steps.heading: Check available storage
steps.body: Open Settings → System → Storage and make room if the system drive is nearly full. Remove only files you recognize; back up important data before deleting personal files.

steps.heading: Run the Windows Update troubleshooter
steps.body: Open Settings and search for Troubleshoot settings. Run the Windows Update troubleshooter if available in your Windows version, then follow its recommended actions.

steps.heading: Repair system files
steps.body: Open Terminal or Command Prompt as administrator and run DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth. When it finishes, run sfc /scannow. Let each command complete before restarting.

steps.heading: If the error continues
steps.body: Write down the exact error code and search Microsoft Support for that code and your Windows version. Avoid third-party driver-updater utilities and do not disable security software permanently.

takeaway: Record the exact error code before trying advanced fixes.

title: How to Fix Wi-Fi Not Working on Windows
description: Find out whether the problem is your router, Windows settings, or the wireless adapter.
intro: When Wi-Fi stops working, first identify whether other devices can connect. This helps separate a router or internet issue from a problem on one PC.

steps.heading: Test another device
steps.body: Connect a phone or another computer to the same Wi-Fi. If all devices are offline, restart the router using its normal power procedure and contact your internet provider if needed.

steps.heading: Toggle Wi-Fi and Airplane mode
steps.body: Make sure Airplane mode is off and Wi-Fi is on. Disconnect and reconnect to the network, then restart the PC.

steps.heading: Forget and reconnect
steps.body: In Settings → Network & internet → Wi-Fi → Manage known networks, select your network and choose Forget. Reconnect with the correct password.

steps.heading: Run network diagnostics
steps.body: Use Windows network troubleshooting from Settings. If the issue began after a driver update, check Device Manager and consider the manufacturer’s supported driver.

steps.heading: Reset networking only later
steps.body: A network reset can remove saved adapters and settings. Use it only after simpler checks and make sure you know your Wi-Fi password and any work VPN requirements.

takeaway: If several devices lose internet at once, investigate the router or service before changing Windows drivers.

title: How to Free Up Storage on an Android Phone
description: Recover space safely without deleting photos, chats, or files you still need.
intro: A nearly full Android phone may slow down, fail to install apps, or struggle to save photos. Check what is using space before removing anything.

steps.heading: Check storage usage
steps.body: Open Settings and look for Storage. Menu names differ by phone maker and Android version. Review which categories use the most space.

steps.heading: Review large downloads
steps.body: Open your Files app and inspect Downloads and large files. Delete only files you recognize and no longer need. Back up important documents first.

steps.heading: Clear an app cache carefully
steps.body: Settings → Apps → choose an app → Storage & cache → Clear cache may remove temporary files. Avoid Clear storage or Clear data unless you understand it can remove local settings, sign-ins, and offline content.

steps.heading: Back up photos and videos
steps.body: Confirm photos are backed up to a service or computer before removing local copies. Verify the backup from another device or browser first.

steps.heading: Remove unused apps
steps.body: Uninstall apps you no longer use and review offline downloads inside streaming, map, and music apps. Restart the phone and check storage again.

takeaway: Clear cache is different from Clear storage. Back up important files before deleting data.

title: How to Fix an Android App That Keeps Crashing
description: Try updates, a restart, cache cleanup, and other low-risk fixes for unstable apps.
intro: An app may crash because of a temporary bug, an outdated version, low device storage, or corrupted temporary data. Try these steps in order.

steps.heading: Restart the phone
steps.body: Close the app and restart your device. Reopen the app to see whether the issue was temporary.

steps.heading: Update the app
steps.body: Open Google Play and install available updates for the affected app. Also check for Android system updates.

steps.heading: Check storage and permissions
steps.body: Free up storage if the device is nearly full. Open Settings → Apps → the app and check permissions relevant to its features.

steps.heading: Clear the cache
steps.body: In the app’s storage settings, choose Clear cache if available. Avoid Clear data unless you have confirmed the app’s data is backed up.

steps.heading: Reinstall if necessary
steps.body: Confirm login details and backup status before uninstalling. If many users are affected, check the app developer’s status or support page.

takeaway: Before reinstalling, make sure app-only files or drafts are backed up.

title: Google Chrome Won’t Open: Troubleshooting Steps
description: Use safe checks to diagnose Chrome startup problems on a Windows computer.
intro: If Chrome will not open, it may be stuck in the background, affected by an extension, or blocked by a damaged profile. Try the simplest checks first.

steps.heading: Check for a background process
steps.body: Restart the computer and try Chrome again. If it still does not open, use Task Manager to check whether Chrome processes remain stuck.

steps.heading: Test another browser
steps.body: Open another browser to confirm your internet connection works. If other browsers also fail, troubleshoot the network or Windows rather than Chrome alone.

steps.heading: Update or repair the installation
steps.body: Use Windows Settings → Apps to check Chrome’s installation. Download the installer only from Google’s official Chrome website if reinstalling is necessary.

steps.heading: Consider extensions and profile data
steps.body: Back up important bookmarks and confirm sync status before making profile changes. An extension or profile issue may be involved.

steps.heading: Check security alerts
steps.body: Review Windows Security notifications and recent software changes. Do not turn off protection permanently or download unofficial repair tools.

takeaway: Use official Google downloads and back up bookmarks before removing profile data.

title: How to Uninstall a Program on Windows 10 and 11
description: Remove unwanted desktop apps using Windows settings or the application’s own uninstaller.
intro: Uninstalling through Windows is usually safer than deleting a program folder manually. Labels can vary by Windows edition and app type.

steps.heading: Use Settings
steps.body: Open Settings → Apps → Installed apps (Windows 11) or Apps & features (Windows 10). Find the application and choose Uninstall.

steps.heading: Follow the app uninstaller
steps.body: Read prompts carefully. Some programs ask whether to keep preferences or local data. Back up files you want to retain.

steps.heading: Use Control Panel for older software
steps.body: For some traditional desktop programs, open Control Panel → Programs → Programs and Features, select the program, and choose Uninstall or Change.

steps.heading: Restart and verify
steps.body: Restart if requested. If an app fails to uninstall, use the publisher’s official support instructions rather than deleting registry entries or system folders.

takeaway: Do not manually delete program folders as a substitute for uninstalling.

title: How to Take a Screenshot on Windows
description: Learn keyboard shortcuts and built-in tools for capturing a window, region, or full screen.
intro: Windows includes several ways to capture your screen. Choose the method that fits whether you need a quick copy, a saved image, or part of the display.

steps.heading: Capture a selected area
steps.body: Press Windows + Shift + S to open the snipping overlay on supported Windows versions. Choose a capture mode.

steps.heading: Capture the full screen to a file
steps.body: Press Windows + PrtScn on supported devices to save a screenshot automatically. Look in Pictures → Screenshots. Some laptops require Fn.

steps.heading: Copy a window
steps.body: Use Alt + PrtScn on supported setups to copy the active window, then paste into Paint, a document, or a chat.

steps.heading: Share safely
steps.body: Check screenshots for passwords, private messages, account numbers, or other sensitive information before sharing.

takeaway: Review screenshots for private information before posting them publicly.

title: Simple Ways to Improve Browser Privacy
description: Review browser permissions, extensions, and account security without installing questionable tools.
intro: A few careful browser settings can reduce unwanted tracking and help protect accounts. Privacy controls vary by browser, so use official help for your version.

steps.heading: Review site permissions
steps.body: Check which websites can access location, camera, microphone, notifications, and pop-ups. Remove permissions you no longer need.

steps.heading: Remove extensions you do not recognize
steps.body: Review installed extensions and remove ones you do not use or cannot verify. Install extensions only from the official store.

steps.heading: Keep the browser updated
steps.body: Install updates from the browser’s built-in update mechanism. Updates often include security fixes.

steps.heading: Strengthen important accounts
steps.body: Use unique passwords and enable multi-factor authentication where available. Be careful with unexpected sign-in links and attachments.

steps.heading: Review shared devices
steps.body: On shared computers, sign out of accounts and avoid saving passwords in profiles other people can access.

takeaway: Avoid privacy-cleaner downloads from unfamiliar sites; built-in settings are a safer start.
